messages.author: 5063972801d34964
messages.subject: Heckman model
parts:
Any suggestions for how to implement a “Heckman” model, along the lines of what is coded up here in Stan by Rob Trangucci (https://discourse.mc-stan.org/t/heckman-selection-model-code-simulation/4853) and discussed further here from a mathematical standpoint: http://rlhick.people.wm.edu/stories/econ_407_notes_heckman.html?

 

It’s a interesting problem because it requires multiple likelihoods (probit-binomial and gaussian), which should not be a problem for INLA generally speaking, but also requires borrowing a transformation of an error term from the other likelihood, not merely sharing or copying a covariate, the method for which is fairly well established at this point.

 

Jonathan

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Heckman model
parts:
Thanks Jonathan for your quick response.  This is a general issue I am struggling with INLA's joint modeling technique and approach -- endogeneity or selection.  

 Like you, I have estimated this Heckman selection type joint mle model using Sampleselection package in R or by writing my own likelihood function with R's Optimum.  My attempt to replicate them using INLA has not been successful. In any case, my interest to use INLA is to take advantage of its flexibility in adding spatial component to my Heckman and/or simultaneous models. So far, I am stuck and no luck!

Secondly, I deal a lot with endogeneity (e.g., Instrumental variable technique or control function modeling  to deal with the endogeneity of  y2 in a model like -- y1 = f(X,y2,u)) or selection bias issues (e.g., Heckman's joint mle model -the topic of current conversation) in my models, and using INLA has not been successful.  R and many other packages can deal with these models (non-spatial versions), but I would love to do them in INLA. 

 Best,
Alok
